findings: A MIXED-DOMAIN SEAMLESS ROW HAS NO TRANSLATIONAL PHASE VARIABLE — AND NEITHER DOES C-0086's UNIFORM ONE. A seamless raster row's two ends ARE the tile edges and both carry a scaffold crossover, so both end columns are pinned; a rigid translation by any non-zero amount takes one of them off the edge. The admissible translation group is {0} at 110 bp and at 112 bp alike, enumerated over every base-pair translation rather than argued. F1 did not fire.

SO C-0090's "TWO PHASES" IS ONE COLUMN LATTICE AND A PARITY BINARY, AND THAT IS THE REFRAMING THIS TASK EXISTS TO REPORT. At 38.08 nm exactly 2 of C-0015's 32 phases put both row ends on a column — 8 and 24, C-0090's own two — and they give IDENTICAL column positions to 1e-12 nm with INVERTED parities at all eight columns. C-0015's phase is a freedom of a tile whose row ends are not crossovers: at the nominal 40.00 nm 10 of 32 phases carry eight columns, and seamlessness spends every one of them. What survives is a binary. F2 did not fire.

AND THE BINARY IS NOT COSMETIC — IT IS THE FACE THE ARMS POINT OUT OF. One column pitch is two 8 bp planes, so shifting by it exchanges a duplex's EAST and WEST azimuths: the upward station lattice of one parity is the DOWNWARD lattice of the other, they partition the plane lattice, and their station counts differ (52 against 53 on the 110 bp row). C-0090 measures the cost without naming it: 0.0621469 of the stroke at phase 8 against 0.0706938 at phase 24, a factor of 1.138. It is CLAUDE.md's "reflecting an out-of-plane array moves it to the other face of the sheet", read as a design variable rather than as a warning.

THE CENSUS. The 110 bp twist-corrected row admits 21 arrangements of its two 15 bp domains, EVERY ONE of which carries eight columns — an identity, columns = domains + 1, where the uniform lattice's count is a function of the phase — 3 of them have a centro-symmetric column set, and there are 12 distinct up to reflection. With the parity binary that is 42 column lattices against the 112 bp row's TWO, of which 6 are centro-symmetric and therefore enumerable by C-0063's family at all. F3 and F4 did not fire.

THE ARRANGEMENT AXIS IS NEW AT 110 bp AND IT DID NOT EXIST AT 112. A uniform row has exactly ONE arrangement, so every phase, placement and centro-symmetry result in this corpus is written on a lattice with no arrangement freedom at all. The twist correction does not merely move the columns; it opens a design variable of 21 members where there was one, and closes a phase variable of 32 that seamlessness had already closed.

A CENTRO-SYMMETRIC COLUMN SET AND A CENTRO-SYMMETRIC STATION LATTICE ARE DIFFERENT CONDITIONS, AND C-0063's FAMILY NEEDS THE SECOND. Of the 21 arrangements 3 have a centro-symmetric column set and 6 have a centro-symmetric STATION lattice under one offset convention or the other, giving 7 enumerable (arrangement, convention) lattices where selecting on column symmetry finds three. Every column-symmetric arrangement is station-symmetric under the MIRRORED convention and NONE of them is under the plain one; 3 further arrangements whose columns are NOT centro-symmetric are station-symmetric at the PLAIN 8 bp offset, where the whole azimuth departure is 4.2857 deg: 15+16+16+16+16+15+16; 16+15+16+16+15+16+16; 16+16+15+15+16+16+16. So C-0133's 30 deg station is a cost of its ARRANGEMENT, not of the twist correction. F7 did not fire.

AND THE FLATNESS RANKING IS A PROPERTY OF THE STATE IT IS READ AT. Under the corrected graded field the flattest of the enumerated lattices is 110 bp 16+15+16+16+16+15+16, mirrored offsets, parity 0 at 0.0580196 and the worst is 0.1843394; at ZERO prestrain the winner is 110 bp 15+16+16+16+16+15+16, plain 8 bp offsets, parity 0 at 0.0552788. C-0133 selects its arrangement on the PEAK REGISTER ANGLE, and that selection is vindicated by the flatness under the field it was made for and REVERSED without it. CLAUDE.md's "quote it with the state it is read at", read on a lattice rather than on a load.

THE PARITY BINARY COSTS ALMOST WHAT IT COSTS ON THE UNIFORM ROW, WHICH IS THE PROOF THAT IT TRANSFERS. On C-0133's recommended lattice the other parity dishes 0.0751454 against 0.0580196 under the corrected graded field — a factor of 1.295 — where C-0090's two phases at 38.08 nm differ by 1.138. Same object, same size, one lattice non-uniform and one uniform.

THE WIDER SHELL IS 1918 ARRANGEMENTS AND IS NOT ADOPTED. Rothemund's own remedy is domain lengths adjusted "by single bases", i.e. {15,16} at a nominal 16; allowing {14..17} gives 1918 compositions, and every extra base pair of spread costs 34.2857 deg of per-domain register where the whole correction is worth 8.5714. The family is a convention and it is stated rather than searched.
